VERDICT: FAIL

- BLOCKER: [session-end-team-teardown.js](C:/Users/Vlad/Desktop/Claude/Projects/WarpOS/scripts/hooks/session-end-team-teardown.js:35) trusts `event.cwd` as `projectDir`, then loads code from that path via `require(.../scripts/teams/lifecycle.js)` and calls `teardown`. If `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` is absent or attacker-controlled, hook input can redirect module loading and teardown requests to a foreign project. Anchor `projectDir` to this hook’s repo root, canonicalize it, and only treat `event.cwd` as corroborating context.

- MAJOR: [mode-lifecycle-guard.js](C:/Users/Vlad/Desktop/Claude/Projects/WarpOS/scripts/hooks/mode-lifecycle-guard.js:107) accepts repo-writable marker files `.mode-guard-off` and `.mode-guard-bootstrap` as unauthenticated kill switches. Any actor with workspace write access can suppress lifecycle telemetry now and bypass the gate after the blocking flip. Require operator attestation outside agent-writable scope, or a signed/owned marker with audit logging.

- MINOR: [mode-lifecycle-guard.js](C:/Users/Vlad/Desktop/Claude/Projects/WarpOS/scripts/hooks/mode-lifecycle-guard.js:199) treats a team member cwd that is a parent of the project as belonging to this project via `normProject.startsWith(c + "/")`. That can mislabel a broad/foreign team as active for this project. The safer scoped test is exact project cwd or member cwd under the project, not parent containment.
